Description: Additive antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects substantially increase bleeding risk.
Management: Avoid unless specifically indicated; if combined monitor INR and watch for bleeding.

Description: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants through platelet inhibition and GI irritation.
Management: Prefer paracetamol for analgesia; if an NSAID is required use gastroprotection and monitor closely.

Description: Regular high-dose paracetamol may potentiate the anticoagulant effect.
Management: Occasional use is acceptable; monitor INR with sustained high doses.

Description: Azole antifungals inhibit warfarin metabolism and markedly raise INR.
Management: Reduce warfarin dose and monitor INR frequently during and after the course.

Description: Increases anticoagulant effect and bleeding risk.
Management: Choose an alternative antibiotic where possible; otherwise monitor INR closely.

Description: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition causes very high statin exposure and risk of rhabdomyolysis.
Management: Suspend the statin for the duration of the antibiotic course.

Description: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition markedly increases the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
Management: Do not co-administer; suspend the statin or use an alternative antifungal.

Description: Amlodipine raises simvastatin exposure and myopathy risk.
Management: Limit simvastatin to 20 mg daily when combined.

Description: Both are antifolates; the combination can cause severe myelosuppression.
Management: Avoid; use an alternative antibiotic.

Description: NSAIDs reduce methotrexate clearance and increase toxicity.
Management: Avoid at antineoplastic doses; monitor closely at low doses.

Description: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance and can cause lithium toxicity.
Management: Avoid where possible; if combined monitor lithium levels.

Description: Thiazide diuretics reduce lithium clearance and raise serum levels.
Management: Monitor lithium concentrations and adjust the dose.

Description: Combining an MAOI with an SSRI risks life-threatening serotonin syndrome.
Management: Do not combine; observe the required washout period between agents.

Description: Additive serotonergic effect increases the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
Management: Avoid if possible; otherwise use the lowest dose and counsel on warning signs.

Description: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and reduces conversion of clopidogrel to its active form.
Management: Prefer pantoprazole if acid suppression is needed.

Description: Amiodarone raises digoxin concentrations and can cause toxicity.
Management: Halve the digoxin dose and monitor levels.

Description: Diuretic-induced hypokalaemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity.
Management: Monitor potassium and replace as needed.

Description: Combined potassium retention can cause dangerous hyperkalaemia.
Management: Monitor serum potassium and renal function regularly.

Description: Risk of lactic acidosis if renal function deteriorates after contrast.
Management: Withhold metformin around the procedure per local protocol.

Description: CYP1A2 inhibition causes a large rise in tizanidine levels with marked hypotension and sedation.
Management: Do not co-administer.

Description: Allopurinol blocks azathioprine metabolism causing profound myelosuppression.
Management: Reduce the azathioprine dose substantially or avoid the combination.

Description: Amiodarone inhibits warfarin metabolism and raises INR for weeks.
Management: Reduce the warfarin dose and monitor INR during and after amiodarone.

Description: Additive negative effects on heart rate and conduction risk bradycardia and heart block.
Management: Avoid combined use; monitor closely if unavoidable.
